source_claim: AlphaEvolve parallelizes expensive candidate evaluation and runs an asynchronous controller, LLM sampler, and evaluator-node pipeline optimized for throughput; Section 2.4 describes spending on the order of 100 compute-hours on a new solution while parallelism preserves generation cadence for consecutive mutations
claim_boundary: This boundary records that LibreEvolve has runtime reporting for configured local stage sample-worker fan-out, observed wall-clock compression, and distributed-pipeline topology linkage. Opt-in candidate evaluation now uses a bounded local asyncio queue, named workers, queue backpressure telemetry, out-of-order completion records, deterministic submission-order result merge and archive admission, exact in-flight duplicate coalescing, and serial shared-state commit. It does not claim AlphaEvolve-style 100-compute-hour candidate budgets, generation-cadence preservation under slow feedback, per-candidate compute-hour budgets, concurrent LLM sampler queues, distributed evaluator nodes, randomized initialization shards, cross-generation proposal/evaluation overlap, mutation-chain depth impact under slow feedback, pending-work resume, or equal-budget parallelism reports.
